info.name: Lab 5 shift
info.description:
A full shift through the Gateway on the Lab 5 stack (#170): login, the shift start as the saga shift.start (Session, University Record, Discord DMs, coordinated by the Message Broker), a ruleset read twice through the Gateway's cache (MISS, then HIT), applicant, chat, decision, end, a second start with the Discord DMs failure switch (409 SHIFT_START_FAILED, the session back in the lobby, no channel left, the saga compensated), the logout and the 401 after it, an ETL run with its row counts, and the monitoring. Run the folders in order inside student-id-net, since the failure switch and the ETL are called directly:

docker run --rm --network student-id-net -v "$PWD/postman:/etc/newman" postman/newman:6-alpine run lab5-shift.postman_collection.json --env-var service_token=<SERVICE_TOKEN> --env-var grafana_password=<GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD>

Uses the seeded players repeat_offender and rookie_one (password seed-password), as the Lab 4 shift does; every run leaves them out of any session, so it can run again.

item.name: Clean up: no armed failure switch is left behind

exec: // The switch counts its arms ($inc). When the start above did not reach create-channels (no saga), the arm is still
// there and would fail the next run's step: send the step on a throwaway saga until one goes through (at most 5), and
// the request itself compensates that saga, so nothing is left behind.
const header = [{ key: "Content-Type", value: "application/json" }, { key: "X-Service-Token", value: pm.collectionVariables.get("service_token") }];
return JSON.stringify({ saga_id, saga_type: "shift.start", step: "create-channels", payload: {
const fire = () => pm.sendRequest({ url, method: "POST", header, body: { mode: "raw", raw: step() } }, (err, res) => {
if (!err && res.code === 500 && tries < 5) { console.log("fired a leftover arm of the failure switch"); fire(); }
pm.test("status 200: the throwaway saga is compensated", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
